# Optical polarizability {.unnumbered #optical-polarizability-theory}

## Response functions {#polarizability-response-functions}

The optical readout follows the scalar, vector, and tensor response functions of Mathur, Tang, and Happer [@mathur1970]. The application displays:

- (alpha_{\mathrm{eq}}): equilibrium isotropic response;
- (alpha_{\mathrm{hfs}}): scalar hyperfine-dependent response;
- (alpha_{\mathrm{gt}}(F,F)): rank-1 vector response;
- (alpha_{\mathrm{br}}(F,F)): rank-2 tensor response.

For each response, the real part is dispersive and the imaginary part is absorptive.

## Polarizability operator {#polarizability-operator}

The ground-state polarizability is represented as an operator-valued Cartesian tensor:

$$
\boldsymbol\alpha
=\boldsymbol\alpha^{(0)}
+\boldsymbol\alpha^{(1)}
+\boldsymbol\alpha^{(2)}.
$$

The vector term contains the antisymmetric tensor coupled to atomic orientation. The tensor term contains a traceless symmetric quadrupole coupled to alignment.

## Tensor normalization {#tensor-normalization}

The Atomic polarizability page displays Mathur's normalized rank-2 coefficient. The optical readout converts it to the raw Cartesian convention

$$
Q_{ij}=\frac12(F_iF_j+F_jF_i)
-\delta_{ij}\frac{F(F+1)}{3}.
$$

For manifold (F), the conversion factor is

$$
c_F=-\sqrt{\frac{30}
{F(F+1)(2F-1)(2F+1)(2F+3)}}.
$$

This sign and normalization are essential for the LDOR contribution discussed in [CBOR and LDOR](cbor-and-ldor.qmd).
